definitions.explanation: A large retail store carrying a wide variety of goods organized into departments. The formal term for what is more casually called デパート.

examples.japanese: ⟦{駅前|えきまえ}→駅前：09593_ekimae⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{百貨店|ひゃっかてん}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{買|か}い{物|もの}→買い物：00853_kaimono⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦した→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: I shopped at the department store in front of the station.

examples.japanese: ⟦{老舗|しにせ}→老舗：16152_shinise⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{百貨店|ひゃっかてん}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{閉店|へいてん}→閉店：09698_heiten⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧ことになった。
examples.english: A long-established department store is going to close.

examples.japanese: {百貨店|ひゃっかてん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{地下|ちか}→地下：03429_chika⟧⟦{食品|しょくひん}→食品：03247_shokuhin⟧⟦{売|う}り{場|ば}→売り場：01331_uriba⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、⟦いつも→いつも：00599_itsumo⟧⟦{賑|にぎ}わっている→賑わう：14235_nigiwau⟧。
examples.english: The basement food floor of the department store is always bustling.

notes:
USAGE:
More formal than the commonly used loanword ⟦デパート→デパート：01022_depaato⟧. Often used in news, business contexts, and official names. Major Japanese department stores include {三越|みつこし}, {伊勢丹|いせたん}, {高島屋|たかしまや}, and {大丸|だいまる}. The ⟦{地下|ちか}→地下：03429_chika⟧⟦{食品|しょくひん}→食品：03247_shokuhin⟧⟦{売|う}り{場|ば}→売り場：01331_uriba⟧ (basement food hall), nicknamed ⟦デパ{地下|ちか}→デパ地下：08828_depachika⟧, is a distinctive feature of Japanese department stores.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {百貨店|ひゃっかてん}⟦{業界|ぎょうかい}→業界：13129_gyoukai⟧ (department store industry)
- ⟦{大手|おおて}→大手：12171_oote⟧{百貨店|ひゃっかてん} (major department store)
- {百貨店|ひゃっかてん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{売|う}り{上|あ}げ (department store sales)
